title: First Trimester Nutrition Checklist: Folate, Iron, and Safer Foods
excerpt: Prioritize folic acid, iron-rich foods, hydration, and cooked foods during weeks 1–12
content:
## Introduction to First Trimester Nutrition

During the first trimester, the mother's body needs to be provided with adequate nutrients to support the development of the fetus. One of the most important nutrients is folic acid, which helps prevent neural tube defects in the fetus. Additionally, iron and other nutrients play a crucial role in the development of the fetus.

## Folic Acid: A Crucial Nutrient

Folic acid is a crucial nutrient during the first trimester. It helps prevent neural tube defects in the fetus, including spina bifida and anencephaly. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), pregnant women should take 400 micrograms of folic acid per day. Foods rich in folic acid include leafy greens, fruits, and whole grains.

## Iron: An Essential Nutrient

Iron is an essential nutrient during the first trimester. It helps support the development of the fetus and prevents anemia in the mother. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), pregnant women should take 27 milligrams of iron per day. Foods rich in iron include red meat, chicken, fish, and legumes.

## Safer Foods

During the first trimester, the mother needs to be careful when choosing foods to ensure safety for the fetus. Foods need to be cooked thoroughly to prevent bacterial contamination. According to the CDC, pregnant women should avoid eating:

* Raw or undercooked foods
* Foods containing listeria
* Foods containing salmonella

## Sample Meal Plan

Here is a sample meal plan for pregnant women during the first trimester:

* Breakfast: oatmeal with fruit and milk
* Lunch: chicken with brown rice and steamed vegetables
* Dinner: grilled fish with roasted vegetables and quinoa

## Conclusion

Nutrition during the first trimester is crucial to support the development of the fetus. Pregnant women need to prioritize folic acid, iron, and other nutrients to ensure health for both mother and baby. Additionally, pregnant women need to be careful when choosing foods to ensure safety for the fetus. For more information on prenatal nutrition, you can visit our [pregnancy meal planner](/planner) page.

## When to Seek Help

If you have any questions or concerns about nutrition during pregnancy, you should seek help from a healthcare provider or a registered dietitian. They can provide you with specific information and guidance to ensure health for both mother and baby. You can also visit our [support](/support) page for more information.
